topic: Post-selection-valid welfare–divergence frontier bands for benchmark-centered assignment rules. In an iid bounded-outcome causal model with overlap, finitely many actions, and a fixed finite-dimensional benchmark-centered softmax class, index the best rule by a KL preference c in a positive compact interval. Assume a unique uniformly interior optimizer with a uniformly negative Hessian and cross-fitted doubly robust nuisance conditions. Prove a joint uniform influence expansion and Gaussian limit for the optimizer, welfare, and benchmark-divergence paths, consistently estimate the covariance kernel, and validate a conditional multiplier bootstrap. Construct a simultaneous confidence tube for the two-coordinate welfare–divergence frontier that remains valid after any measurable choice of c from the plotted curve; use set-valued inversion at tangencies or self-intersections. Jointly calibrate the n-scaled penalized-regret process through its Hessian quadratic form. Credit Fang–Ridder–Xie arXiv:2512.19230v3 for fixed-preference efficiency and their three-arm commitment-savings frontier. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The score-blind presolve derived the joint influence maps for the optimizer, welfare, and divergence, the penalized cancellation identity, and the uniform quadratic-regret reduction. It solved the binary-covariate three-action witness exactly, established a uniform curvature lower bound 0.0026816936, and numerically checked influence centering and frontier derivatives. Vanishing penalties, weak overlap, redundant logits, localization, selected-index limits, constrained inversion, estimated scale, and oracle-versus-implemented welfare were checked; generic indexed-inference results cap novelty but no exact collision was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove conditional multiplier replacement and tightness for fold-specific estimated stacked influences evaluated along the same-sample optimizer path, using shrinking empirical-L2 error and uniform entropy bounds. EARLY KILL TEST: On the twelve-atom witness at c=.5,1,2, verify influence centering, penalized cancellation, H theta-prime=-grad K, and the quadratic regret expansion, then check held-out nuisance linearization and multiplier covariance errors; a persistent root-n remainder or failed identity stops the run. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_kl_frontier_postselection_band.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish a joint uniform influence expansion and conditionally valid multiplier bootstrap for the benchmark-centered softmax optimizer, welfare, and KL-divergence paths over a compact positive preference interval when fold-specific estimated influence functions are evaluated along the same-sample optimizer path.

source_refs.claim: The paper treats each positive KL weight as fixed in its efficiency theory, reports the estimated welfare-divergence frontier descriptively, and does not supply simultaneous frontier inference.
source_refs.author: Yue Fang, Geert Ridder, Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: This paper constructs simultaneous confidence bands for function-valued Z-estimation targets using approximately orthogonal scores and an estimated-score multiplier bootstrap.
source_refs.author: Alexandre Belloni, Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Ying Wei

source_refs.claim: DML uses Neyman-orthogonal scores and cross-fitting for root-n inference with learned nuisances, primarily for fixed low-dimensional targets rather than an optimizer-indexed curve.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Mert Demirer, Esther Duflo, Christian Hansen, Whitney Newey, James Robins

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fang–Ridder–Xie derive fixed-preference optimizer and regret limits and plot a grid of frontier points, while their nuisance-remainder arguments are local to one optimizer. Belloni et al. supply generic functional Z-estimation bands, but the unresolved step is uniform replacement for the random class formed by fold-specific nuisance estimates composed with the same-sample argmax path. That step requires shrinking empirical-L2 influence error, a deterministic uniform entropy envelope, stochastic equicontinuity, and covariance-kernel consistency for the stacked optimizer, welfare, and divergence process. Searches for benchmark-centered softmax multiplier bootstrap, welfare-divergence frontier confidence bands, and cross-fitted optimizer-path inference found the fixed-weight paper and generic DML/band machinery but no theorem covering this composition.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem in the product space l-infinity(C) giving a uniform asymptotically linear representation and tight Gaussian limit for c mapped to (theta_c, W_c, K_c), uniform covariance-kernel consistency, and conditional weak convergence of the estimated-influence multiplier process sufficient for a simultaneous tube valid after every measurable selection of c.

writing_exemplar.why: Mirror its institutional motivation for preserving a benchmark lottery and its progression from a KL-penalized rule to a welfare-divergence menu, then present uncertainty for the whole menu as the inferential gap.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Existing lotteries carry procedural or learning value -> KL-penalized softmax tilts improve welfare while remaining near the benchmark -> the preference weight indexes a plotted welfare-divergence menu -> a decision maker choosing from that menu needs simultaneous post-selection-valid inference

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their uniform Bahadur representation for orthogonal function-valued Z-estimators and estimated-score multiplier bootstrap, proving their entropy and replacement conditions for the optimizer-composed cross-fitted class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both targets are continua of orthogonally estimated parameters requiring simultaneous Gaussian approximation, but the desired result stacks an implicit argmax with two smooth causal functionals.

method_exemplars.technique: Use their Gaussian coupling and multiplier-bootstrap bounds for empirical-process suprema after placing the random estimated-influence class inside a deterministic entropy envelope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The tube critical value is a supremum of a vector empirical process; their coupling machinery supplies the final conditional approximation once nuisance replacement and tightness are established.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift the foldwise conditional-mean-zero decomposition and product-rate control for Neyman-orthogonal cross-fitted scores from a fixed target to a Lipschitz-indexed optimizer path.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nuisance-error mechanism is cross-fitted double robustness; the new burden is uniformity after composing the score with theta-hat(c).

open_problems.open_problem: Jointly calibrate the entire n-scaled penalized-regret path with the root-n optimizer and welfare-divergence paths by proving a uniform Hessian-quadratic reduction and a conditionally valid corrected multiplier bootstrap for its supremum and other path functionals.

source_refs.claim: For a fixed positive preference weight, penalized-welfare regret multiplied by n converges to one half of a Gaussian quadratic form involving the criterion Hessian.
source_refs.author: Yue Fang, Geert Ridder, Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: For first-order-degenerate smooth functionals with a nonzero second derivative, the standard bootstrap is generally inconsistent and requires a second-order correction or modified bootstrap.
source_refs.author: Qihui Chen, Zheng Fang

source_refs.claim: This paper supplies multiplier-bootstrap Gaussian couplings for suprema of empirical processes with increasing complexity.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Denis Chetverikov, Kengo Kato

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fang–Ridder–Xie establish the quadratic regret law pointwise in the preference weight, whereas simultaneous frontier use requires one Gaussian optimizer process G(c), one estimated Hessian path H(c), and uniform control of the Taylor remainder. Regret is first-order degenerate at every optimum, so Chen–Fang's result warns that an ordinary recentered bootstrap need not reproduce the quadratic limit. The missing argument is a uniform second-order delta method coupled to estimated cross-fitted influence paths, Hessian plug-in control, and anti-concentration for sup_c G(c)'H(c)G(c). Searches for uniform quadratic-regret processes and policy-frontier Hessian-form bootstraps found pointwise policy-regret laws and generic quadratic-functional bootstrap theory but no indexed frontier calibration.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint weak-convergence theorem for (sqrt(n)(theta-hat-theta), sqrt(n)(W-hat-W), sqrt(n)(K-hat-K), nR-hat) in a product function space, with nR-hat(c)=G(c)'H(c)G(c)/2+o_p(1) uniformly, plus a corrected multiplier scheme consistently estimating quantiles of suprema and integrated functionals of the quadratic process.

writing_exemplar.why: Retain its decision-theoretic message that first-order estimation variance creates second-order welfare regret, then move from one preference to simultaneous statements about the full menu.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The chosen rule is root-n noisy -> optimality cancels first-order penalized-welfare loss -> regret survives at the n scale as a Hessian quadratic form -> choosing c from a frontier requires joint calibration of that quadratic-form path

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their second-order delta method and derivative-composition bootstrap correction to the function mapping c to penalized regret.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Penalized regret has a zero first derivative at the optimizer and a nonzero Hessian, exactly the first-order-degenerate structure for which the ordinary bootstrap can fail.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine their coupling and anti-concentration tools for process suprema with a continuous quadratic mapping and uniform plug-in control of H(c).
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired critical value concerns a supremum of a non-Gaussian quadratic transform of a Gaussian process; their multiplier Gaussian coupling supplies the transferable first layer.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct honest set-valued inversion of a simultaneous two-coordinate welfare-divergence frontier tube when the restricted softmax path has tangencies, repeated frontier points, or self-intersections, so that all preference values compatible with a welfare-divergence target are covered simultaneously.

source_refs.claim: The paper notes that divergence in a restricted finite-dimensional assignment class need not be one-to-one in the preference weight, motivating a frontier rather than a single implied weight.
source_refs.author: Yue Fang, Geert Ridder, Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: This paper obtains simultaneous inner and outer confidence sets for inverse images by inverting simultaneous confidence intervals, including protection against data peeking across multiple levels.
source_refs.author: Junting Ren, Fabian J. E. Telschow, Armin Schwartzman
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series C

source_refs.claim: This paper constructs a simultaneous sausage-shaped confidence region for a smooth one-dimensional curve embedded in a multidimensional space.
source_refs.author: Hiroya Yamazoe, Kanta Naito

open_problems.why_unsolved: The source-method direction is to transport inverse-set confidence-set logic to a causal frontier indexed by a preference parameter. The first proof step that changes is the passage from scalar-band inversion or an embedded curve with unique local normal coordinates to the inverse correspondence of a possibly noninjective vector path. At a tangency the derivative loses the rank required by ordinary delta-method localization, while at a self-intersection multiple disjoint c-branches map to the same point. The frontier is additionally produced by a cross-fitted optimizer rather than direct regression. Searches combining welfare-divergence frontiers with inverse sets, tangencies, and self-intersections found generic inverse-set and embedded-curve methods but no causal-policy result handling these geometries.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A random-closed-set theorem giving simultaneous inner and outer confidence correspondences for C(B)={c in C:(W(c),K(c)) in B}, with asymptotic coverage for points, rectangles, and constrained frontier regions without injectivity or nonzero-derivative assumptions.

writing_exemplar.why: Use its shadow-price interpretation of c and its warning that the restricted frontier need not be one-to-one to motivate correspondence-valued rather than scalar inversion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A proximity constraint has an interpretable shadow price c -> restricted softmax classes can map several c values to the same or locally tangent frontier geometry -> a plotted confidence tube does not identify which preferences support a desired point -> inference must return the full compatible preference set

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their deterministic inversion of simultaneous bands into inner and outer inverse confidence sets, replacing scalar preimages by the inverse correspondence of a bivariate causal path.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is an inverse set protected against data peeking, but the target set is generated by a noninjective estimated policy frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their simultaneous tubular-region construction for a curve in R^2, replacing unique normal-coordinate arguments near an embedding with branchwise unions and rank-adaptive neighborhoods.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The displayed welfare-divergence frontier is a one-dimensional curve in two dimensions, while tangencies and self-intersections are the geometry excluded by a standard embedded-curve treatment.

method_exemplars.technique: Use their Gaussian-process strong approximation and adaptive inequality selection when inversion is represented as continuum intersection bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Branchwise constraints defining compatible preference values can be expressed as intersections of inequalities, providing a robust route when direct local inversion is singular.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the local-to-zero KL-penalty transition for benchmark-centered assignment rules and develop inference that remains valid as an interior softmax optimizer approaches a deterministic or boundary treatment rule.

source_refs.claim: The paper separates fixed positive penalties, where the optimizer is regular and interior, from the zero-penalty boundary, where deterministic assignment is nonregular.
source_refs.author: Yue Fang, Geert Ridder, Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: This paper develops local asymptotic decision theory for statistical treatment rules when treatment choice is a nonregular function of underlying parameters.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano, Jack R. Porter

source_refs.claim: This paper compares nonsmooth empirical welfare maximization with a smoothed welfare maximizer and derives distinct regret rates for threshold policies.
source_refs.author: Federico Crippa

open_problems.why_unsolved: The positive-penalty and zero-penalty literatures describe opposite endpoints but do not identify the intermediate rate regimes for c_n tending to zero. Along those sequences, softmax probabilities approach simplex faces, the Hessian can lose uniform curvature, and overlap-weighted influence envelopes may grow. The first Fang–Ridder–Xie proof step to fail is inversion of a uniformly nonsingular Hessian; the inverse can diverge and the second-order regret normalization can change. Hirano–Porter's limit-experiment analysis and Crippa's smoothing arguments supply adjacent machinery, but searches for local-to-zero KL treatment-rule asymptotics and vanishing entropy-penalty causal inference found endpoint results rather than a semiparametric transition theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A phase-diagram theorem indexed by the rate of c_n relative to n that gives optimizer and regret normalizations, limiting laws, and a confidence procedure uniformly valid over specified regular-interior, weak-curvature, and deterministic-boundary regimes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its regular-positive versus nonregular-zero dichotomy frames the missing bridge as a boundary of the paper's scope.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A positive KL weight preserves randomized interior assignment -> reducing the weight permits larger welfare-improving tilts -> at zero the target becomes a hard nonregular policy -> practitioners need to know where the regular approximation fails as the preference approaches zero

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their local asymptotic experiment and risk analysis for discontinuous treatment choice to sequences of smooth softmax rules whose penalty shrinks toward the discontinuity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination limit is the same nonregular treatment-choice problem, approached through a regularized path rather than imposed at the outset.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the comparison of smoothed and unsmoothed welfare maximizers and its rate calculations, using KL temperature as the smoothing sequence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems ask how a smooth policy approximation changes regret rates as it approaches a hard assignment boundary.

open_problems.open_problem: Extend simultaneous welfare-divergence frontier inference to benchmark-centered rules learned from adaptively collected randomized experiments, allowing predictable assignment probabilities and controlled but possibly diminishing exploration.

source_refs.claim: The benchmark-centered analysis uses iid data from a fixed benchmark and does not provide inference for adaptively collected data.
source_refs.author: Yue Fang, Geert Ridder, Haitian Xie

source_refs.claim: This paper uses adaptive variance-stabilizing weights for AIPW policy evaluation and obtains asymptotically valid confidence intervals under adaptive experiments.
source_refs.author: Vitor Hadad, David A. Hirshberg, Ruohan Zhan, Stefan Wager, Susan Athey
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.claim: This paper develops generalized AIPW policy learning with adaptively collected data and proves minimax regret bounds, including under diminishing exploration.
source_refs.author: Ruohan Zhan, Zhimei Ren, Susan Athey, Zhengyuan Zhou

open_problems.why_unsolved: The donor method is Hadad et al.'s predictable variance-stabilized AIPW martingale construction; the destination is an optimizer-indexed KL frontier rather than evaluation of a fixed policy. The first proof step that changes is replacement of the iid empirical-process expansion by a uniform martingale-array expansion whose predictable variance kernel depends jointly on c, the learned optimizer path, and adaptive logging probabilities. Zhan et al. handle adaptive policy learning through regret bounds rather than simultaneous post-selection frontier inference. Searches for adaptive-experiment welfare-divergence bands and adaptive benchmark-centered multiplier bootstraps found adaptive fixed-policy evaluation and regret results but no joint optimizer, welfare, and divergence tube.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A predictable-design theorem giving a uniform martingale influence representation and Gaussian or stable limit for the optimizer, welfare, and divergence paths, a consistent predictable covariance estimator, and a valid wild or multiplier-bootstrap tube under explicit exploration-rate conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing makes adaptive assignment a deliberate design for final policy choice, providing the natural destination narrative for a benchmark-proximity frontier under sequential learning.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fixed randomization wastes opportunities to learn while treating -> adaptive experiments shift probability toward promising actions while retaining exploration -> the terminal planner still faces a welfare-versus-departure preference menu -> that menu needs simultaneous design-aware inference

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their predictable adaptive weighting of AIPW summands and self-normalized martingale CLT, proving variance stabilization uniformly over the preference index.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly solves causal policy-value inference under adaptive assignment; the new structural layer is optimization and joint frontier indexing.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over adaptive weighting that controls exploding importance weights when target and logging policies differ, then establish a functional rather than scalar studentized limit.
method_exemplars.why_closest: KL-tilted frontier policies can depart variably from the logging design across c, matching the policy-dependent weight-instability problem addressed by adaptive off-policy evaluation.

method_exemplars.technique: Use generalized AIPW weighting and exploration-dependent regret control to establish optimizer consistency before deriving the martingale influence process.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest adaptive-data policy-learning result, but the desired resolution replaces a regret bound with simultaneous inference for a smooth preference-indexed causal frontier.

literature_map:
1. Fang, Ridder, and Xie (2026, arXiv:2512.19230v3) define benchmark-centered KL-penalized assignment, derive fixed-positive-preference efficiency and pointwise quadratic regret, and plot a three-arm commitment-savings welfare-divergence frontier without simultaneous inference.
2. Their key scope boundary is that the preference weight is fixed in the theory while the displayed frontier varies it; restricted classes can also make divergence noninjective in that weight.
3. Kitagawa and Tetenov (2018, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA13288) and Athey and Wager (2021, Econometrica, arXiv:1702.02896) anchor empirical welfare maximization and doubly robust policy learning, primarily through regret rather than confidence tubes for a smooth policy path.
4. Chernozhukov et al. (2018, Econometrics Journal, arXiv:1608.00060) supply orthogonal-score and cross-fitting logic for root-n causal inference, chiefly for fixed low-dimensional targets.
5. Belloni, Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Wei (2018, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1512.07619) provide the closest generic result: simultaneous bands for function-valued orthogonal Z-estimators via an estimated-score multiplier bootstrap.
6. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014/2016, Annals of Statistics and SPA, arXiv:1212.6885 and arXiv:1502.00352) provide Gaussian coupling, anti-concentration, and multiplier-bootstrap tools for empirical-process suprema.
7. Firpo, Galvao, and Parker (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1911.10215) treat uniform inference for optimized value functions using directional derivatives, highlighting nonstandard behavior introduced by marginal optimization.
8. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey (2024, QJE, DOI 10.1093/qje/qjad043) and Wei et al. (2024, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2206.11868) show that selecting an apparently best option creates winner's-curse failures and motivates selection-aware or simultaneous guarantees.
9. Ren, Telschow, and Schwartzman (2024, JRSS C, arXiv:2210.03933) invert simultaneous bands into inner and outer inverse sets protected against data peeking, but do not treat a noninjective causal frontier generated by an estimated optimizer.
10. Yamazoe and Naito (2024, CSDA, DOI 10.1016/j.csda.2023.107891) construct simultaneous regions for embedded curves; their geometry is a close analogue but does not cover self-intersecting optimizer-generated frontiers.
11. Chen and Fang (2019, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1901.04861) show that ordinary bootstrap inference can fail for nonzero second-order functionals under first-order degeneracy, warning against naive bootstrapping of quadratic regret.
12. Hirano and Porter (2009, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA6630) and Crippa (2025, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:2404.11767) describe the nonregular hard-policy endpoint and smoothing-dependent regret, leaving the local-to-zero KL transition unresolved.
13. Hadad et al. (2021, PNAS, arXiv:1911.02768) establish adaptive-weight AIPW confidence intervals for policy evaluation, while Zhan et al. (2021, KDD, arXiv:2106.02029) control policy-dependent importance-weight instability.
14. Kasy and Sautmann (2021, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA17527) and Zhan, Ren, Athey, and Zhou (2024, Management Science, arXiv:2105.02344) study adaptive design and adaptive-data policy learning, but not simultaneous welfare-divergence frontier bands.
15. Exact-pair searches located no paper jointly combining cross-fitted same-sample optimizer paths, a bivariate KL-frontier tube, arbitrary post-plot preference selection, set-valued inversion, and uniform calibration of the n-scaled quadratic-regret process.
